abstract: Every aspect of messenger RNA life and fate is dictated by its complementary bound proteins. RNA-binding proteins (RBPs) regulate mRNA localization, translation, and/or degradation, and mRNAs encoding functionally related proteins can form "RNA regulons" that are bound by shared sets of RBPs. Here, we present an open-source multi-colour smFISH-based workflow we developed to systematically quantify mRNA abundance and localization across the budding yeast cell cycle. With this workflow, we investigate the cell-cycle dependent regulation of mRNAs encoding cell wall proteins (cwmRNAs) in Saccharomyces cerevisiae yeast. We quantify the localization of SRL1 and SUN4 cwmRNAs which are bound by Ssd1, Mpt5/Puf5, and She2-She3 among other RBPs. We show that SRL1 and SUN4 exhibit distinct cell cycle-dependent abundance and localization patterns, and that SRL1 mRNA relies on She2 and She3 and partially Ssd1, but not Mpt5, for its localization to the bud. Our results argue that Ssd1 and Mpt5 are not primarily RNA localization factors and confirm the importance of the She2-She3 complex in conferring bud-localization to diverse mRNAs. We also show that SUN4 and SRL1 mRNA localization is not affected by the Sec complex which facilitates the localization of their protein products. These findings show that co-regulated mRNAs can follow distinct spatiotemporal programs, and our workflow provides a general framework to test how RNA-binding proteins coordinate mRNA localization in single cells.
